The page is empty." - wait: 1200 - caption: "v-for on the li: one li for each name in the list." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

In Vue you write the tag **once**: ```html

  • ` tags to match. `v-if` shows a tag only while something is true: ```html

    No players yet.

    ``` ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict insight: "Students from the DOM course expect a changed array not to change the page; in Vue it does, which is the point of v-for." check: type: predict q: "You click Add Kai once. How many names are on the page?" options: ["4", "3: changing the array does not change the page", "1", "6"] actual: "4. push adds Kai to players, and v-for makes an li for every item, so a fourth li appears." ``` In the DOM course, pushing to an array did not change the page. What about here? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 440 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I emptied the list and saw the No players yet message appear." } ``` Press **Run**. Add Kai, then remove players until none are left, and watch the message. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "v-for repeats the tag it is on, once per item; v-if adds or removes its tag as its condition changes; both follow the data." tasks: - check: type: trace text: "Start with Ada, Sam and Lin. Fill in the page after each click." table: | | after | li tags on the page | No players yet shows? | | the start | 3 | no | | Add Kai | [4] | [no] | | Remove the last, four times | [0] | [yes] | | Add Kai | [1] | [no] | explain: "The page always matches the list: one li per item, and the message only while the list is empty." - check: type: match q: "Match each part with what it does." pairs: - ["v-for=\"name in players\"", "makes this tag once for each item"] - ["{{ name }}", "the item for this copy of the tag"] - ["v-if=\"players.length === 0\"", "shows this tag only while the list is empty"] - ["players.push('Kai')", "adds an item to the end of the list"] explain: "v-for and v-if go on the tag they control. The data decides how many copies there are and whether the tag shows." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "The page shows three separate lists, each with one name. There is no error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: vue-for-parent explain: "v-for repeats the tag it is written on. On the ul, it makes three lists. Put it on the li: one list, three items." ``` ### Trace the page Count the tags. ### Which part does what? v-for, v-if and the item. ### Spot the bug Three lists instead of one. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "A new button changes the list; a new v-if reacts to a new condition." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 440 } tasks: - hint: - "Emptying the list means giving players a new, empty list." - "``" expected: page.html#sol-clear check: { type: code, text: "Add a Clear button that empties the list.", rules: { contains: ["Clear"] } } - hint: - "A second v-if can look for a different number." - "`

    = 5\">Team full!

    `" expected: page.html#sol-full check: { type: code, text: "Show Team full! when there are 5 or more players.", rules: { contains: ["Team full"] } } ``` ### Clear the list One button, an empty list. ### Team full A second v-if. ## Make: a playlist ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: a v-for list, a v-if message, and buttons that change the list." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 440 } check: { type: code, text: "Show the songs with v-for, a message with v-if when there are none, and buttons that change the list.", rules: { contains: ["v-for", "v-if", "@click"] } } ``` Show the **songs** as a list with `v-for`, a message with `v-if` when there are none, and buttons that **add** a song and **remove** one (`push`, `pop`, or `shift`, which takes the first). ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "Your team page should add whatever name someone types, not always Kai. What does it need?" options: ["A box joined to some data, and a function that adds it", "A longer v-for", "A second list", "A v-if on the button"] answer: 0 explain: "Next lesson: v-model joins a box to data, and a function in setup does the adding." ``` Next: **events and inputs**: functions on clicks, and boxes joined to data. ```teacher summary: Students predict that pushing to a list adds a tag, trace the page as the list changes, find v-for on the wrong tag, add a Clear button and a Team full message, and make a playlist. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can make a tag for each item in a list with v-for. - I can show a tag only when something is true with v-if. - I can change a list and watch the page keep up. before: > Read the unit primer first. `v-for="name in players"` on a tag makes one copy of that tag per item; inside it, `name` is the item for that copy. `v-if="…"` adds the tag while the condition is true and removes it otherwise. Both are **attributes on the tag they control**, which is why the planted bug (v-for on the `ul`) makes three lists. This reverses the DOM course's lesson on lists, where changing an array did not change the page ("list-is-live"). In Vue it does, because the list is a ref. Say so explicitly to students who did the DOM course; it is a good moment to name what Vue is doing for them. Real Vue code adds `:key` to v-for tags (`:key="name"`) so Vue can tell items apart when they move; it does not change what students see here, so the course leaves it to the stretch. `players = []` inside `@click` works because the page unwraps refs for you (lesson 3 shows the script side). running: - "Predict: ask DOM-course students what happened when they pushed to an array there." - "Run: empty the list and ask what made the message appear." - "Investigate: do the trace on paper first, then check it by clicking." - "Modify: for Team full, ask which number to compare and with which sign." - "Make: ask each student to say which tag v-for repeats." struggle: Students put v-for on the container because "it's the list". Ask "which tag do you want more of?" and let them move it themselves. stuck: - see: Several lists, each with one item. ask: Which tag has the v-for? fix: Put v-for on the li, not the ul or ol. - see: The message never shows or never goes. ask: What does the v-if compare, and is it === ? fix: v-if="players.length === 0"; a single = sets a value instead of comparing. - see: The names show as {{ name }}. ask: Is the li inside the div with id app? fix: "Keep everything Vue should handle inside #app." stretch: Add :key="song" to the v-for. Number the items with v-for="(song, i) in songs" and {{ i + 1 }}. Add v-else after a v-if. support: Give the ul with v-for already written; students add only the v-if message. leads: "Next lesson: functions for events and v-model for inputs, so the list can take any name. Class idea: find three lists on a website and say what each item's data would be." exit: q: Why does v-for go on the li and not the ul? a: v-for repeats the tag it is on, once per item; we want many li tags in one list, not many lists. explain: | 1. The data is a list of three players; the page starts empty. 2. `v-for` on the `li` makes one `li` for each name in the list. 3. A button adds Kai to the list. 4. Change the list, and Vue adds the `li` for you. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-clear step-4#t2: page.html#sol-full step-5: page.html#sol-make sources: - title: "Vue.js: List rendering (v-for)" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/list.html checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "Vue.js: Conditional rendering (v-if)" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/conditional.html checked: 2026-10-12 ```
